value_domain: Synthetic person-level identifier
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The person key that ties a migrant's demographic record to their address history and to the rest of the asset. It is the only join between the three demographic tables, which hold one row per person, and the three address tables, which hold one row per address episode, so the relationship between them is one to many. In the live asset the equivalent key is produced by the ABS Person Linkage Spine, which "allows us to link datasets through a spine of key information, separate from the main body of data"; here the value is generated and carries no meaning outside this package.
value_definition: An opaque person-level identifier repeated on every row belonging to that person. It encodes nothing about visa, arrival, birth or residence, and is not ordered.
limitation: It marks a person in the asset, not a migrant in Australia. The same key appears for someone who was granted a visa and never arrived, for someone who has since left, and for an Australian-born citizen carried in the client information source, so selecting on the presence of a row is not a migrant population. Counting rows in the address tables also counts moves, not people.
rationale: The ABS PLIDA page describes the Person Linkage Spine that supplies the person key in the live asset, and the six migrant and traveller demographic tables use this column as their sole cross-table join.
evidence_quote: allows us to link datasets through a spine of key information, separate from the main body of data
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's wording, 'Synthetic person level identifier', with one generic sentence printed as both value definition and limitation, so it did not say that the key is one to one on the demographic tables and one to many on the address tables.

value_domain: SACC country of birth code
value_source: ABS, Standard Australian Classification of Countries (SACC)
variable_description: The country the visa holder was born in, coded to the ABS country classification rather than left as the country name on the travel document. The classification is the SACC, which "provides guidelines for consistent collection, aggregation and dissemination of statistics by country" and which the ABS endorses for exactly this use, birthplace. Country of birth is fixed for life, so unlike CNTRY_CDE on the address tables it does not change from row to row.
value_definition: A four-digit SACC code. "Countries have four-digit codes where the first two digits represent the parent minor group code and the final two digits represent the sequence of countries within a minor group". There are 255 country categories, four of them residual, grouped into 27 minor groups and 9 major groups.
limitation: Not every code in this column is a country. SACC keeps four-digit supplementary codes beginning '000' for inadequate data, '0000' for unintelligible responses and '0003' for 'not stated', and codes beginning '09' for defunct political entities such as '0913 Former Yugoslavia, nfd', so a straight frequency count mixes real countries with these. Country of birth is also not citizenship and not the country a person migrated from: a person born in one country may have lived in a second and arrived from a third.
rationale: The SACC is the classification the ABS applies to birthplace across the asset and the page gives both the code structure and the supplementary codes that a user of this column has to know about.
evidence_quote: The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) endorses the use of this classification when collecting, aggregating and disseminating data relating to characteristics such as birthplace and country of residence.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's wording, 'Visa holder birth country', with the same generic sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it did not name the classification, the code width, or the supplementary codes that are not countries.

value_domain: SACC country code for the address
value_source: ABS, Standard Australian Classification of Countries (SACC)
variable_description: The country the address on this row is in, which is how an overseas address is carried in a table otherwise built for Australian geography. It uses the same classification as birthplace, the SACC, which the ABS endorses for "birthplace and country of residence" alike. Where the value is not Australia, the mesh block, SA1, SA2, SA4 and state columns on the same row have nothing to hold, because the ASGS only covers Australia.
value_definition: A four-digit SACC country code attached to an address episode rather than to a person, so one person can hold several values over time as their recorded address moves between countries.
limitation: It is where the department held an address, not where the person was living. An agent's address, a sponsor's address or an address left unchanged after a move all produce a country code that outlives the person's presence there, and a person physically in Australia can carry an overseas country code for a period. The same '000' inadequate-data and '09' defunct-entity supplementary codes apply here as to birthplace, so not every value names a current country.
rationale: The SACC page states the classification's endorsed use for country of residence and gives the code structure, which is what this column carries; the neighbouring ASGS columns in the same table fix why the country code matters.
evidence_quote: The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) endorses the use of this classification when collecting, aggregating and disseminating data relating to characteristics such as birthplace and country of residence.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording, 'Country of residence', with one generic sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it did not say the code sits on an address episode or that non-Australian values leave the geography columns empty.

value_domain: Address episode start date
value_source: ABS, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: The day the address on this row became the department's effective address for the person, opening one episode in an address history that reaches back to 1990. Rows line up per SYNTHETIC_AEUID into a sequence, so a person's moves are read as consecutive start and end dates rather than as a single current address. The records behind it are the Home Affairs client information holdings that the ABS describes as "Client information on Australian-born citizens, temporary & permanent migrants".
value_definition: A calendar date opening an episode, paired with END_DATE on the same row. Episodes for one person are meant to run in sequence, and the geography columns on the row describe the address for the span between the two dates.
limitation: It dates a departmental record, not a move. The start date is when the address took effect in the department's system, which follows the person actually moving by however long it took them to notify Home Affairs or to lodge a form that carried the new address, so short tenancies can be missed entirely and a move can appear months late. Episodes from different feeding systems can also overlap, so a person may have two open addresses at once rather than a clean sequence.
rationale: The ABS page for PLIDA data names the Home Affairs client information collection that this address table is built from and its reference period, which establishes what kind of event the effective date records.
evidence_quote: Client information on Australian-born citizens, temporary & permanent migrants.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's wording, 'Effective address start date', with the same generic sentence twice over, so a reader was not warned that the date belongs to the administrative record rather than to the person's move.

value_domain: Address episode end date
value_source: ABS, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: The day the address on this row stopped being the department's effective address for the person, closing the episode that START_DATE opened. It is what makes the address tables a history rather than a snapshot: to place a person somewhere on a given day you select the episode whose start and end dates straddle that day. The underlying records are the Home Affairs client information holdings the ABS describes as "Client information on Australian-born citizens, temporary & permanent migrants".
value_definition: A calendar date closing an episode. The current address for a person is the episode with no end date, or with an end date set far in the future, depending on how the extract was cut.
limitation: A missing end date does not mean the person still lives there. It means the department has not recorded a replacement address, which is equally consistent with the person having left Australia, died, or simply never told anyone they moved. The end date is likewise the day the record was superseded, not the day the person moved out, so an episode length is a record length and should not be read as a duration of residence.
rationale: The ABS page for PLIDA data identifies the Home Affairs client information source behind this table, which fixes the effective end date as a record event; the episode structure is visible in the table's own columns.
evidence_quote: Client information on Australian-born citizens, temporary & permanent migrants.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave only the custodian's wording, 'Effective address end date', and printed one generic sentence as both value definition and limitation, so the meaning of a blank end date was left for the reader to guess.

value_domain: Sex or gender of the visa holder
value_source: ABS, Standard for Sex, Gender, Variations of Sex Characteristics and Sexual Orientation Variables
variable_description: The visa holder's recorded sex or gender, as it appears on the 2021 vintage of the migrant demographics table. The ABS standard treats the two as different concepts, since "Gender is a social and cultural concept" while "Sex recorded at birth refers to what was determined by sex characteristics observed at birth or infancy", and this column carries whatever single value the department holds rather than an answer to either standard question. The 2023 and 2025 vintages of the same table call the column SEX, so the change of name between extracts is not evidence that the underlying item changed.
value_definition: A single categorical value per person, conventionally male, female and a small residual. The ABS standard codes sex as 1 Male, 2 Female and 3 Another term, and gender as 1 Man or male, 2 Woman or female, 3 Non-binary, 4 Different term and 5 Prefer not to answer; a departmental field will usually resolve to the binary.
limitation: It cannot tell you which concept was captured. The value comes from a visa application or a travel document, so it reflects what a passport authority recorded and what the applicant could enter on a form at the time, and it will not identify a person whose gender differs from the sex on their document. Comparing counts across the 2021, 2023 and 2025 table vintages also compares a column called GENDER with one called SEX, which is a naming change and not a re-collection.
rationale: The ABS standard defines the two concepts and their response categories, which is what a reader needs to interpret a single departmental field that is labelled gender in one extract and sex in the next.
evidence_quote: Gender is a social and cultural concept. It is about social and cultural differences in identity, expression and experience as a man, woman or non-binary person.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's wording, 'Visa holder gender', with the value definition and the limitation carrying the same generic sentence, so nothing flagged that the neighbouring vintages call the same item SEX.

value_domain: Sex of the visa holder
value_source: ABS, Standard for Sex, Gender, Variations of Sex Characteristics and Sexual Orientation Variables
variable_description: The visa holder's recorded sex, on the 2023 and 2025 vintages of the migrant demographics table. The ABS standard defines the concept narrowly: "Sex recorded at birth refers to what was determined by sex characteristics observed at birth or infancy", which is not what a visa system captures, since its value comes from a passport or an application form. The 2021 vintage of the same table calls this column GENDER, so the two names cover one departmental item across extracts.
value_definition: A single categorical value per person. The ABS standard response categories are 1 Male, 2 Female and 3 Another term, and the ABS notes that "most ABS surveys will only output the binary responses to a sex question (Male or Female)".
limitation: It is a document field, not an observation and not an identity. Where a person's passport shows a value they no longer use, or where a jurisdiction records a third option, this column shows the administrative value and no history of change. It also carries no imputation flag, so a value that was supplied by default rather than recorded cannot be told apart from one that was.
rationale: The ABS standard states what sex recorded at birth means and lists the response categories the ABS uses, which is the yardstick against which a departmental sex field in an ABS-held asset has to be read.
evidence_quote: Sex recorded at birth refers to what was determined by sex characteristics observed at birth or infancy.
supersedes_rationale: The entry repeated the custodian's wording, 'Visa holder sex', and printed one generic sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it neither gave the categories nor connected the column to GENDER in the 2021 vintage.

value_domain: Registered marital status
value_source: ABS, Census dictionary 2021, Registered marital status (MSTP)
variable_description: The visa holder's marital status, on the 2021 vintage of the migrant demographics table. It is taken from departmental records rather than asked as a survey question, and the concept matches the ABS one, which "records a person's formal registered marital status" in the categories never married, widowed, divorced, separated and married. The 2023 and 2025 vintages carry the same item under the shortened name MARITAL_STS, whose own label in the metadata is misspelt 'Martial status'.
value_definition: A single categorical value per person. The ABS categories for the same concept are 1 Never married, 2 Widowed, 3 Divorced, 4 Separated, 5 Married and @ Not applicable, the last for persons under 15 years.
limitation: It has no date attached, so it is a status at an unknown moment. The value is whatever the department last recorded, usually at a visa application or a change of circumstances notification, which means marriages, separations and divorces after that point are invisible and the column cannot be lined up with a Census night or a payment date. A de facto relationship is also not a registered status, so partnered people appear here as never married.
rationale: The ABS Census dictionary gives the definition and the closed category set for registered marital status, which is the classification the integrated asset uses when it holds a marital status field.
evidence_quote: This variable records a person's formal registered marital status. If registered marital status is not stated, it is imputed.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's wording, 'Marital status', with the same generic sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it gave neither the categories nor the warning that the status carries no date.

value_domain: Registered marital status

variable_description: The visa holder's marital status on the 2023 and 2025 vintages of the migrant demographics table, and the same item that the 2021 vintage carries as MARITAL_STATUS. evidence_quote: This variable records a person's formal registered marital status. If registered marital status is not stated, it is imputed.

value_domain: ASGS Mesh Block code (2021 column vintage)
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026
variable_description: The Mesh Block the address on this row falls in, carried by the 1990-2023 extract of the migrant address table. The ABS defines it as the smallest ASGS area, holding 30 to 60 dwellings in most cases: "Mesh Blocks (MBs) are the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS and form the building blocks for the larger regions of the ASGS. Most Mesh Blocks contain 30 to 60 dwellings." The code describes the address episode between START_DATE and END_DATE, not the person, so somebody with four address episodes has four of these codes.
value_definition: An ASGS Edition 3 Mesh Block code, assigned by geocoding the address the department held. The ASGS main structure nests mesh blocks into SA1s, SA1s into SA2s, and so on up through SA3s and SA4s to states and territories, so the geography columns on one row are all descriptions of one point.
limitation: The mesh block is small enough to be disclosive on its own, so it is normally used to build larger areas rather than to report on. It also identifies a block, not a dwelling: a mesh block containing an apartment tower holds hundreds of households, so two people sharing a mesh block are not neighbours in any useful sense and certainly not a household.
rationale: The ASGS Edition 3 page is the ABS's own definition of the geography level this column codes to and of the nesting between levels that the other geography columns on the same row rely on.
evidence_quote: Mesh Blocks (MBs) are the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS and form the building blocks for the larger regions of the ASGS. Most Mesh Blocks contain 30 to 60 dwellings.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's terse wording and printed the same generic sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so it said nothing about the size of the area, the edition of the geography, or the fact that the code belongs to an address episode.

value_domain: ASGS state and territory code (2021 column vintage)
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026
variable_description: The state or territory the address on this row sits in, held as a number, on the 1990-2021 and 1990-2023 extracts of the migrant address table. In the ASGS, "States and Territories (S/T) are a cartographic representation of legally designated state and territory boundaries", built up from mesh blocks like every other level on the row. It is the coarsest of the geography columns and the one most likely to survive when the finer ones are missing.
value_definition: A single-digit ASGS state and territory code, 1 New South Wales through to 8 Australian Capital Territory, with codes 9 and above for other territories and for a non-Australian or unknown location depending on the extract.
limitation: A present state does not mean a coded address. Where the address could not be geocoded the state can still be filled from other information, and IMPUTED_STATE on the same row is the flag that says so, so a state distribution that ignores that flag mixes coded and imputed values. The state is also the state of the recorded address, not a state of usual residence on any statistical definition, and it says nothing about how long the person was there.
rationale: The ASGS Edition 3 page defines the state and territory level and its place in the main structure, which is what this numeric column codes; the registry shows which table vintages carry the imputation flag beside it.

value_domain: ASGS state and territory code (2022 column vintage)
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS) Edition 3, July 2021 - June 2026
variable_description: The state or territory the address on this row sits in, held as a number, on the 1990-2025 extract of the migrant address table. In the ASGS, "States and Territories (S/T) are a cartographic representation of legally designated state and territory boundaries", built up from mesh blocks like every other level on the row. It is the coarsest of the geography columns and the one most likely to survive when the finer ones are missing.
value_definition: A single-digit ASGS state and territory code, 1 New South Wales through to 8 Australian Capital Territory, with codes 9 and above for other territories and for a non-Australian or unknown location depending on the extract.
limitation: A present state does not mean the address was coded. The 2025 table drops the IMPUTED_STATE flag that the earlier tables carry, so on this vintage there is no way to tell a state derived from a geocoded address from one carried over or filled in. The value is also the state of a departmental address record rather than a state of usual residence, and it cannot be read as time spent in the state.
rationale: The ASGS Edition 3 page defines the state and territory level and its place in the main structure, which is what this numeric column codes; the registry shows which table vintages carry the imputation flag beside it.
evidence_quote: States and Territories (S/T) are a cartographic representation of legally designated state and territory boundaries.
supersedes_rationale: The entry showed the custodian's wording, 'State (number)', with the same generic sentence printed as both value definition and limitation, so it did not say which classification the number belongs to or that some values are imputed.

value_domain: Flag that state was imputed rather than coded from the address
value_source: ABS, Overseas Arrivals and Departures, Australia methodology, June 2024
variable_description: A flag marking the address rows whose state was filled in rather than derived from a coded address. No published document defines the flag, but the ABS fills a missing state or territory of residence in its other Home Affairs-sourced statistics: for overseas arrivals and departures it says "An additional alternate source used for state or territory of residence is Medicare enrolment data" before any statistical imputation is applied. The flag appears on the 2021 and 2023 vintages of the address table and not on the 2025 vintage, so the same check cannot be made on the latest extract.
value_definition: A binary indicator attached to an address episode, set where STATE_ASGS on the same row did not come from geocoding the recorded address. It qualifies the state column and no other geography column on the row.
limitation: It is not a quality score and not an error flag. An imputed state can be right and a coded state can be stale, so the flag tells you the provenance of one value and nothing about whether the person was in that state. It also does not say what the imputation used, so records flagged here cannot be graded by how strong the inference behind them was, and dropping them removes a non-random group, concentrated among people with thin administrative footprints.
rationale: The ABS methodology for the overseas arrivals and departures collection documents how the ABS fills a missing state or territory of residence for Home Affairs-sourced records, which is the closest documented analogue to what this flag marks; neither the flag nor its code list is published.
evidence_quote: An additional alternate source used for state or territory of residence is Medicare enrolment data
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's wording, 'Flag for state was imputed', with the same generic sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it did not say what the flag qualifies or that the 2025 table has no equivalent.

value_domain: Name of the departmental collection the row came from
value_source: ABS, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: Which departmental collection supplied this row, on both the demographic and the address tables. The Home Affairs holdings in the asset are separate collections with different reference periods and different content: "Client information, from 1984", "Visa Information & Citizenship Grants, from 2000" and "Net Overseas Migration (NOM) Traveller data, from 2004", among others. Because one person can appear from several of them, this column is what tells you why a row exists and which other tables its person is likely to appear in.
value_definition: A short text label naming the feeding collection or system, one value per row. SRC_CD on the address tables carries the coded form of the same idea.
limitation: It ranks nothing. Two rows from different sources can describe the same address or the same person with different values, and this column gives no rule for choosing between them: it is not ordered by recency, by accuracy or by authority, so a conflict has to be resolved on the dates, not the source. It also says nothing about how complete the source is, so a source that appears on few rows may be narrow rather than rare.
rationale: The ABS page listing the data in PLIDA names the separate Home Affairs collections and their start years, which is the set this column distinguishes between; the registry shows the column appearing on all six migrant demographic and address tables.
evidence_quote: All overseas movement records on Home Affairs’ Travel & Immigration Processing System. Movement records are supplied via monthly extracts with the data being compiled on a quarterly basis.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Address source', which is wrong for the three demographic tables that also hold the column, and printed one generic sentence as both value definition and limitation.

value_domain: Coded form of the address source
value_source: ABS, PLIDA data and legislation
variable_description: The coded twin of SOURCE on the three address tables, identifying which departmental record supplied the address on this row. Where SOURCE spells the collection out, this holds the short code the department uses for it, so the two move together and either can be used to split an address history by origin. It appears only on the address tables, not on the demographic tables that carry SOURCE.
value_definition: A short code, one value per address episode. The code frame is the department's own list of address-supplying systems and is not published with the data, so the mapping from code to collection has to be recovered from SOURCE on the same rows.
limitation: A code cannot be carried between table vintages on faith. The three address tables are separate extracts and a code present on the 1990-2021 table cannot be assumed to mean the same collection on the 1990-2025 table, so a series split by SRC_CD should be rebuilt from SOURCE in each. The code is also not a confidence rating: it says where the address came from, not how well it was verified.
rationale: No published document defines this code frame. The ABS page naming the separate Home Affairs collections in the asset establishes what the codes distinguish between, and the presence of SOURCE beside it on every address row establishes that the two are the coded and text forms of one item.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording, 'Address source code', with the same generic sentence as both value definition and limitation, so it did not link the column to SOURCE or warn that the codes are extract specific.

value_domain: Flag for coding to a sub-address within a property
value_source: ABS, ABS Address Register Information Guide
variable_description: A flag on how precisely the address on this row was resolved, marking rows coded to a sub-address within a property rather than to the property alone. The ABS Address Register carries unit-level detail, including unit number and unit type, and its coding services are designed to enable analysis at unit and address level, so a flat in a block can be coded to itself rather than to the building. On this table the flag sits beside the mesh block, SA1, SA2, SA4 and state columns that the address was coded to.
value_definition: A binary indicator attached to an address episode, describing the level the address text was matched at rather than the address itself. It qualifies the geography columns on the same row.
limitation: It is not a test of whether the address is right. A sub-address match can point at the wrong unit and a property-level match can be entirely correct for a house, so the flag describes matching precision and not accuracy. It is also not a dwelling type indicator: a row flagged as a sub-address tells you the coding reached unit level, not that the person lives in a flat, and a person in a flat whose address was written without a unit number will not be flagged at all.
rationale: The ABS Address Register information guide sets out the unit-level address components and the address coding services that make sub-address coding possible, which is the process this flag reports on; no published document defines this column by name.
evidence_quote: Enhanced address matching through the creation of indexes used in ABS Address Coding services enabling finer geospatial analysis at unit/address level.
supersedes_rationale: The entry gave the custodian's wording, 'Address coding sub flag', with one generic sentence printed twice as value definition and limitation, so nothing said what 'sub' referred to.
